main_text.p: anas interpretati fuerint, affirmari potuerunt? Addit Hieronymus, & Judaico quodam Rabbi prohibeat, Ju-dæorum quoddam per Shiloh Messiæ hoc tempus interpretatur, [illegible, ~12 letters] atque ... intelligere videri Judæorum. Aquilas, Ariston, apud Cyrillum fil. 9. in ipsum ac interpretationis suæ nationem non à significatione Grammatica ipsius dictionis, quicquid tandem illa significet, sed ab ... ... ... ... & Scriptura ... ... vare. Hunc autem interpretationem utrumque (Karaitarum scilicet, & Cyrilli) imputabunt, & quæ maxime ... Præterea enim Jacobum non Judæorum calamitatem, sed gloriam, ... ... contrarie patet. Deinde non omnino ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... [illegible, ~10 letters] Hebræus ... Haec (ut ipsi credimus) scribunt, Dux non ... Shiloh, idem, filius Jacobi, feminini generis ... Ita ... ... ... Messiæ ... ... Shiloh à ... Shilo ... ... ... ... ... ... nascitur ... ... ... pro Messiæ ... Ergo ... Gaglerius ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... [illegible, ~8 letters] Shilo ... Messiam ipsum ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... fuisse. Hæc ille, quæ cum à Fagio etiam, ac postea à Gualperio sint citata, nullâ censurâ ... ... ... ... ... ... ... Neque enim de fœminino

page.notes: The scan is very blurred and much of the text cannot be read with certainty. Many lines are only partly legible; I have marked unreadable stretches as illegible and left gaps as "..." only in this notes element, not in the text. The last word of the page, "minino", is set off to the right below the text and is probably the end of "fœminino" (the word is split across the line end). The running head's left element appears to read "Cap. 49o" (possibly a chapter reference) and is not included in the running head. The text is a Latin commentary on Genesis 49 (Shiloh passage). Words in the middle of the page could not be confirmed and may contain errors.
